method.ceiling: best LEAVE-ONE-OUT least-squares over {tAir} and {tAir,rh,wind,cloud,solar}; an out-of-sample upper bound on any model using this forcing. In-sample fits overfit badly at n=12.
method.model: the physical model at its fitted (bound-pinned) parameters

night.why: air temperature explains night surface temperature well (r ~ 0.9), so a calibrated model is meaningful here

day.why: daytime surface temperature depends on site-level insolation, cloud timing and soil moisture that 50 km reanalysis forcing cannot resolve; no model on this data can do better

ward_scale.method: leave-one-OVERPASS-out; scene- and ward-level splits leak through shared overpasses and are not published

domain.ballygunge: data/geometry/kmc-wards-around-ballygunge.geojson ward 68 polygon: 189 of 676 ECOSTRESS pixels (centre inside); surface/built over the polygon's cells

pending_recalibration.reason: the ECOSTRESS evidence set grew after accuracy.ts was written
pending_recalibration.action: recalibrate and update accuracy.ts in a reviewed change; this campaign deliberately does not move published constants
pending_recalibration.published_peak_evidence: accuracy.ts peak n=29 (RMSE 4.42 K, ceiling 3.338 K, band 4.5 K) is an older ECOSTRESS evidence set, scored with Ballygunge as the old 1400 m box; strata.peak_ecostress is the current measurement, with Ballygunge as the KMC Ward 68 polygon

intercomparison.note: underpowered: only 2 ECOSTRESS overpass(es) fall in the 9.5-11.5 h window Landsat occupies, below the 5 needed to call a sensor offset. Daytime strata are published separately and no pooled daytime figure is computed. Comparing outside this window would measure the diurnal cycle, not the instruments.
